jess (Docs): Quick sync thread for the audit-export / retention docs PR I'm preparing. Need alignment on retention defaults, KMS rotation behavior, and a short PII redaction example. PR will include CLI + SDK samples for the v2 export flow.

omar (Security): Thanks. Two quick constraints: 1) avoid words like 'permanent' or 'irreversible' 92; 2) be explicit about key destruction making data unrecoverable. Also call out that retention is configurable per-tenant.

maria (Legal): Agreed. From compliance side we also need an example retention policy and a short note describing how we can demonstrate deletion for auditors (export timestamps + deletion event logs).

jess (Docs): Draft language for review: "Audit exports are retained per the customer's configured retention period (default 180 days). Exports are encrypted using the customer's KMS key. When keys are rotated, previously encrypted exports remain decryptable if the KMS retains prior key versions. If a key is destroyed, data encrypted with that key may be unrecoverable. Customers may request deletion of exports; Redwood logs deletion events to provide an audit trail for compliance requests." Thoughts?

ben (DevEx): Wording looks good. For the migration guide, I'll replace the old CLI examples. Proposed v2 CLI sample: `ri export audit --from 2025-02-01 --to 2025-02-28 --kms-key arn:aws:kms:...:key/my-key --dest s3://acme-exports/feb.ndjson`

rachel (PM): Can we surface a small decision table in the doc that recommends streaming vs batch exports by use-case (ad-hoc investigation vs daily backups)? That will help customers pick the right sample.

jess (Docs): Good idea. I'll add a 3-row table: ad-hoc (streaming, low-latency), analytics (batch, S3), archival (scheduled batch + lifecycle rules).

omar (Security): Redaction guidance: prefer doing PII removal at the source before export. Example snippet for docs: `{"ts":"2025-02-15T12:00:00Z","user_email":"[REDACTED]","action":"api_key_create"}`. Mention hashing as alternate approach for pseudonymization.

maria (Legal): Also include a brief sentence: "Redaction may affect the ability to investigate incidents; choose policy to balance privacy and forensics"

ben (DevEx): Will add curl + python streaming examples. Curl example: `curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v2/audit/export -H 'Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY' -d '{"start":"2025-02-01","end":"2025-02-28","kms_key":"my-key","dest":"s3://..."}'` . Python streaming example will show context manager and incremental processing.

jess (Docs): Note: link checker flagged an internal runbook that the current doc points to. @deploy-bot can you post the canonical runbook URL?

deploy-bot: Canonical runbook now: https://go.redwood/runbooks/audit-exports-v2 8link-id: runbook.audit.exports.v29. I've updated the repo link map entry. :white_check_mark:

rachel (PM): One more: make the retention default explicit but call out that enterprise contracts may set custom minimums. E.g., "default 180 days; enterprise agreements may provision longer retention or different deletion SLAs."

jess (Docs): Will include that sentence. Planning to push the branch in ~30m. @omar @maria can you please review the security/legal blurb and the key-rotation paragraph once I open the PR?

omar (Security): I'll take it after dinner and flag anything critical. If it's just tweaks, I'll approve.

maria (Legal): I'll do a quick read when you're ready. If we need to add an auditor-friendly example of deletion proof (log snippet), I can draft one.

ben (DevEx): After the PR lands I'll add the updated examples to the SDK migration checklist so we don't forget customers using older CLI/SDK versions.

jess (Docs): Thanks all 44b. I'll ping when the PR is up. Keep any micro-phrasing notes inline on the PR for faster iteration.

deploy-bot: PR 4821 created: branch `docs/audit-export-retention-update`. CI: docs-lint ok, link-checker now passes after runbook update. Reviewers requested: maria, omar, ben.

jess (Docs): Awesome, thanks!
